raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

On CUDA, every tensor-parallel rank runs the sparse-attention (DSA) indexer on every decode row: paged MQA logits, DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate selection or mask, and top-k. Every rank ends up with the same indices. At long context this is a large part of the decode step.

This PR adds an opt-in, `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1`, that splits the decode rows across TP ranks:

- **Row assignment:** rank `r` scores the rows of requests `r, r + tp, r + 2·tp, …`. All of a request's rows stay on one rank, because the varlen `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` reads a request's KV once for all of its rows.
- **Metadata builder:** gathers each rank's rows, block-table rows and context lengths into persistent buffers and builds that rank's DeepGEMM schedule. The plan depends only on the padded row count, so CUDA graphs replay with the same buffers.
- **Indexer op:** scores the local rows, keeps DeepSeek-V4.1 candidate blocks rank-local, all-gathers the int32 top-k indices across TP ranks, and restores request order in `topk_indices_buffer`.
- **When it applies:** uniform decode batches with at least `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD_MIN_REQS` requests (default 8), on the varlen paged-logits path, without DCP/PCP or the sparse-logits indexer.

## Test Plan

**Serve.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4× B200. The only difference between main and this PR is `VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD`: `0` behaves exactly like main, `1` is this PR.

```bash
VLLM_DSA_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD=1 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
VLLM_DISABLE_DSV4_MEGAMOE_SHARED_EXPERT_FUSION=0 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name dsv41 --port 8008 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 512
```

**Benchmark.** AIPerf with the InferenceX AgentX traces: long-context, multi-turn agentic sessions with a mean input of ~135K tokens. 64 concurrent sessions, 1,200 s (the concurrency-128 runs use `--concurrency 128`):

```bash
aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp --url http://127.0.0.1:8008 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --endpoint-type chat --streaming --model dsv41 \
  --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --num-dataset-entries 393 \
  --concurrency 64 --benchmark-duration 1200 --random-seed 42 \
  --trajectory-start-min-ratio 0.25 --trajectory-start-max-ratio 0.75 \
  --warmup-requests-per-lane 10 --trace-idle-gap-cap-seconds 300 --warmup-grace-period 1800 \
  --failed-request-threshold 0.10 --use-server-token-count --no-gpu-telemetry
```

Main and this PR ran at the same time on one 8× B200 node: one server on GPUs 0–3, the other on GPUs 4–7.

**Long-context benchmark (`vllm bench serve`).** 64 distinct 126,000-token random prefixes are sent once with 1 output token to fill the prefix cache. Each measured prompt is one of those prefixes (round-robin, so every wave of 64 requests reads 64 different KV histories) plus a fresh 2,000-token random suffix: 128,000 input tokens with 98.4% prefix reuse, 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 64. Both files use the `custom` dataset format, one `{"prompt": ..., "output_tokens": ...}` per line. Main and this PR again ran side by side on one node.

```bash
# 1. Warm the 64 prefixes
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path warm.jsonl --custom-output-len 1 --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
  --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 16 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --temperature 0

# 2. Measure: prefix + fresh 2,000-token suffix
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model dsv41 --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8008 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path measure.jsonl --custom-output-len 1024 --skip-chat-template --disable-shuffle \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 0 --temperature 0 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

**Unit test.**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_decode_row_shard.py
```

## Test Results

AgentX, concurrency 64, 1,200 s. Two runs with main and this PR on swapped GPU groups:

| metric | main (run 1) | this PR (run 1) | main (run 2) | this PR (run 2) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 2,411.6 | 2,508.8 | 2,408.7 | 2,501.1 | **+3.9%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 321,158 | 337,083 | 322,167 | 335,165 | **+4.5%** |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 2.38 | 2.46 | 2.38 | 2.45 | +3.2% |
| TTFT avg / p50 (ms) | 398 / 197 | 368 / 199 | 337 / 198 | 364 / 195 | −0.4% / −0.4% |
| ITL avg / p50 / p90 (ms) | 11.85 / 10.94 / 16.87 | 10.62 / 9.47 / 15.56 | 11.78 / 10.96 / 17.26 | 10.53 / 9.50 / 15.51 | **−10.5% / −13.4% / −9.0%** |
| Output tok/s per user (avg) | 101.6 | 111.7 | 102.3 | 112.3 | +9.9% |

Run 1: main on GPUs 0–3, this PR on GPUs 4–7. Run 2: swapped. Change = mean of the two runs.

AgentX, concurrency 128, 1,200 s. Same two-run layout:

| metric | main (run 1) | this PR (run 1) | main (run 2) | this PR (run 2) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 3,359.7 | 3,422.4 | 3,354.7 | 3,394.2 | +1.5% |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 354,405 | 352,926 | 344,214 | 351,535 | +0.9% |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 3.86 | 3.87 | 3.79 | 3.84 | +0.8% |
| TTFT avg / p50 (ms) | 542 / 316 | 545 / 313 | 552 / 334 | 541 / 322 | −0.8% / −2.3% |
| ITL avg / p50 / p90 (ms) | 34.84 / 37.72 / 47.80 | 34.63 / 38.08 / 47.98 | 36.22 / 39.49 / 51.09 | 34.93 / 38.44 / 48.04 | −2.1% / −0.9% / −2.8% |
| Output tok/s per user (avg) | 39.3 | 40.0 | 37.9 | 39.4 | +2.8% |

At concurrency 128 the gain is small: each step carries far more prefill work (ITL ~35 ms vs ~11 ms at concurrency 64), so the decode indexer is a smaller share of the step.

Long-context prefix reuse (`vllm bench serve`), 128,000 input / 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 64, 512 prompts. Same two-run layout:

| metric | main (run 1) | this PR (run 1) | main (run 2) | this PR (run 2) | change (run 1 / run 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 5,279.8 | 5,701.9 | 7,461.8 | 7,813.3 | +8.0% / **+4.7%** |
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 665,256 | 718,443 | 940,192 | 984,476 | +8.0% / **+4.7%** |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 5.16 | 5.57 | 7.29 | 7.63 | +8.0% / +4.7% |
| TTFT mean (ms) | 2,693 | 2,919 | 1,491 | 1,450 | +8.4% / −2.8% |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 1,181 | 1,409 | 1,286 | 1,321 | +19.3% / +2.8% |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 9.18 | 8.08 | 6.83 | 6.35 | −11.9% / −7.0% |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 24.41 | 20.97 | 24.42 | 21.09 | **−14.1% / −13.7%** |
| Speculative acceptance length | 5.72 | 5.76 | 5.76 | 5.70 | |

Run 1: main on GPUs 0–3, this PR on GPUs 4–7. Run 2: swapped. The prefix-cache hit rate was 98.4% on every server. Run 1 was the first run in a new container, and both arms were about 30% slower than in run 2 (most likely first-use kernel compilation), so run 2 is the steadier comparison. ITL p50, about one decode step, drops 14% in both runs. Throughput gains less because about half of each request's time is spent in steps that also carry prefill, which this PR does not change.

GSM8K accuracy (main vs this PR): to be added.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import (
+    DeepseekV32IndexerDecodeRowShard,
+    decode_row_shard_plan,
+    restore_decode_row_order,
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size", [2, 4, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_reqs,rows_per_req", [(1, 1), (3, 6), (8, 6), (13, 2), (48, 6)]
+)
+def test_decode_row_shard_scores_every_row_once_in_order(
+    tp_size: int, num_reqs: int, rows_per_req: int
+) -> None:
+    """Each decode row is scored by exactly one rank, a request's rows stay
+    together under one id, and the all-gathered results land back in order."""
+    num_tokens = num_reqs * rows_per_req
+    plans = [
+        decode_row_shard_plan(num_tokens, rows_per_req, tp_size, rank)
+        for rank in range(tp_size)
+    ]
+    owned = torch.cat([rows[valid] for rows, valid, _ in plans])
+    assert torch.equal(owned.sort().values, torch.arange(num_tokens))
+    for rows, _, ids in plans:
+        assert ids.numel() == rows.numel() + 1
+        per_req = ids[: rows.numel()].view(-1, rows_per_req)
+        assert (per_req == per_req[:, :1]).all()
+        assert (per_req[1:, 0] != per_req[:-1, 0]).all()
+
+    # What each rank all-gathers: the (valid) row it scored.
+    gathered = torch.cat([rows.masked_fill(~valid, -1) for rows, valid, _ in plans])
+    num_local_reqs = plans[0][0].numel() // rows_per_req
+    row_shard = DeepseekV32IndexerDecodeRowShard(
+        rows=plans[0][0],
+        seq_lens=torch.empty(0),
+        block_table=torch.empty(0),
+        indices=torch.empty(0),
+        schedule_metadata=torch.empty(0),
+        tp_size=tp_size,
+        rows_per_req=rows_per_req,
+        num_local_reqs=num_local_reqs,
+    )
+    restored = restore_decode_row_order(gathered[:, None], row_shard, num_tokens)
+    assert torch.equal(restored[:, 0], torch.arange(num_tokens))

+class DeepseekV32IndexerDecodeRowShard:
+    """This TP rank's share of the decode rows.
+
+    Decode rows are replicated on every TP rank; with row sharding each rank
+    scores the rows of every ``tp_size``-th request (``rows`` into the decode
+    rows, all of a request's rows together so the paged logits kernel reads
+    its KV once) and the ranks all-gather the finished top-k indices.
+    """
+
+    rows: torch.Tensor
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor
+    block_table: torch.Tensor
+    indices: torch.Tensor
+    schedule_metadata: torch.Tensor

+    rows_per_req: int

+def decode_row_shard_plan(
+    num_tokens: int, rows_per_req: int, tp_size: int, rank: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Decode rows that ``rank`` scores: those of requests rank, rank + tp, ...
+
+    Every request is ``rows_per_req`` consecutive rows. Returns (on CPU) the
+    row of each local slot, whether the slot is a real request (padding slots
+    past the last request point at row 0), and a request id per local row
+    with one spare entry, since the paged logits kernel reads ids in pairs.
+    """
+    num_reqs = num_tokens // rows_per_req
+    num_local_reqs = -(-num_reqs // tp_size)
+    req = torch.arange(num_local_reqs) * tp_size + rank
+    valid = (req < num_reqs).repeat_interleave(rows_per_req)
+    rows = (req[:, None] * rows_per_req + torch.arange(rows_per_req)).flatten()
+    ids = torch.arange(num_local_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    ids = ids.repeat_interleave(rows_per_req)[: rows.numel() + 1]
+    return torch.where(valid, rows, 0), valid, ids
+

+    gathered: torch.Tensor,
+    row_shard: "DeepseekV32IndexerDecodeRowShard",
+    num_tokens: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Put rank-ordered all-gathered rows back in decode-row order."""
+    gathered = gathered.view(
+        row_shard.tp_size, row_shard.num_local_reqs, row_shard.rows_per_req, -1
+    )
+    return gathered.transpose(0, 1).reshape(-1, gathered.shape[-1])[:num_tokens]
